2.text: The Kolyma country is ravaged by various diseases, among which syphilis

3.text: and leprosy have attracted most of the attention of the authorities, perhaps

4.text: for the reason that their external forms are so horrible and shocking. The

5.text: town of Sredne-Kolymsk even had a hospital destined for the poorest people

6.text: suffering from these two diseases. No words are adequate to represent fully

7.text: the horrors of this hospital. It stood in the middle of the so-called “Hungry

8.text: Ward” of the town, and was in the shape of a large hut of Yakut style.
8.note: Draft had a literal backslash-quote (\") for the closing quotation mark; printed glyph is U+201D RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK, pairing with the opening “ on the previous line.

9.text: Not only its walls, but even the ground all around it, were soaked with filth.

10.text: The patients were mostly Yakut, all suffering from the worst forms of the

11.text: disease. Only such were brought to this hospital. All the others, if there

12.text: was still a single ray of hope for them, were kept out. I witnessed a case

13.text: where a man suffering from syphilis was brought in from the country. He

14.text: had made a journey of a hundred miles crouched on a small Yakut sledge,

15.text: which was drawn by a saddle-horse attached by means of long traces fastened

16.text: to the saddle-bow, in Yakut fashion. When the assistant surgeon bade him

17.text: strip, he tucked up his fur shirt and showed us a round birch-bark vessel tied

18.text: up to his loins, and filled with completely destroyed tissues. When these

19.text: were cut off, he did not even feel any pain.

20.text: I should add also that the better half of the food destined for the sustenance

21.text: of the sufferers was appropriated by the warden; so that they had to apply

22.text: for alms to private individuals. Sometimes, when their diet ran too short,

23.text: they would send in a threat that they would leave the hospital in a body

24.text: and crawl around from house to house (most of them were unable to walk).

25.text: Then the citizens would pay a ransom to keep them quiet.¹
25.note: Draft read the line-final footnote marker as a literal ']'. Zoomed at 4×: it is superscript '1' (U+00B9), matching the note opener on line 42. §2.10.

26.text: This is the sort of medical assistance that is given to the population in

27.text: the Kolyma country. A surgeon is included on the official staff of the district,

28.text: but his place almost always remains vacant. Those that are occasionally sent

29.text: from Russia find employment much nearer than the Kolyma. Even the

30.text: southern part of eastern Siberia has so little medical assistance, that a real
30.note: A speck above 'of' at 4× is a printing blot, not a mark or letter — no ink shape resembling a diacritic or apostrophe.

31.text: graduated physician is not allowed to pass through into the arctic desert.

32.text: Thus in the Kolyma district there are only non-graduated assistant surgeons

33.text: without knowledge and experience, who go there either on account of the short

34.text: time of service that entitles them to a pension, or half crazy from drinking

35.text: and sent to the Kolyma as a punishment.

36.text: Vaccination has been practised in the Kolyma district for a full century,

37.text: ever since 1806. Young men specially selected for the purpose, the so-called

38.text: “vaccination-boys,” received brief instructions from the assistant surgeon, and
38.note: Draft had a literal backslash-quote (\") for the closing quotation mark after the comma; printed glyph is U+201D, pairing with the opening “.

39.text: travelled from village to village, vaccinating the young and the old. In 1884,

40.text: as soon as the first news came of the small-pox epidemic having broken out

41.text: in the neighboring districts, a small-pox committee was organized, and the
